source_text:
Ὁ λύχνος τοῦ σώματός ἐστιν ὁ ὀφθαλμός.
Ἐὰν οὖν ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ἁπλοῦς ᾖ, ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου φωτεινὸν ἔσται. Ἐὰν
δὲ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου πονηρὸς ᾖ, ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου σκοτεινὸν ἔσται. Εἰ δὲ τὸ φῶς τὸ
ἐν σοὶ, σκότος ἐστὶ, τὸ σκότος πόσον; Ἀπλοῦς ὀφθαλμὸς, ἡ ἀνυπόκριτός ἐστιν ἀγάπη,
δι' ἧς ὅταν τὸ σῶμα φωτίζηται, τὰ αὐτὰ τοῖς ἔσωθεν νοούμενοις, καὶ διὰ τῶν ἔξωθεν
μερῶν προφέρουσα; ὁ δὲ πονηρὸς ὀφθαλμός ἐστιν ἡ προσποίητος ἀγάπη, ἥτις καὶ
ὑπόκρισις καλεῖται· δι' ἧς ἅπαν τὸ σῶμα σκοτίζεται τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
thought_title: The eye as lamp and love as light
orientation: Gregory opens by quoting Matthew 6:22-23, then begins explaining the saying's terms.
pass_a_gloss: The lamp of the body is the eye. If then your eye is sound, your whole body will be full of light. But if your eye is evil, your whole body will be dark. But if the light in you is darkness, how great is the darkness? A sound eye is sincere love, through which, whenever the body is enlightened, it brings forth the same things as the things thought within, also through the outward parts. But the evil eye is pretended love, which is also called hypocrisy; through it the whole body of the man is darkened.

choices.why: Glossary English for the key term; 'sound' captures the sense of healthy and sincere without the banned 'simple' or 'single'.
Glossary English; 'evil' preserves the moral weight Gregory assigns to pretended love.
Glossary English; 'sincere' renders the negation of hypocrisy directly.
Glossary English; 'pretended' keeps the active sense of outward show.
Renders the adjective's force as a state of being illuminated, matching the body's condition.

choices.english: the same things as the things thought within
choices.why: Keeps the comparison explicit: outward words match inward thoughts, which is Gregory's point about sincerity.
rejected: the same as the inner thoughts

bible_refs.note: Ὁ λύχνος τοῦ σώματός ἐστιν ὁ ὀφθαλμός. Ἐὰν οὖν ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου ἁπλοῦς ᾖ, ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου φωτεινὸν ἔσται.
Ἐὰν δὲ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου πονηρὸς ᾖ, ὅλον τὸ σῶμά σου σκοτεινὸν ἔσται. Εἰ δὲ τὸ φῶς τὸ ἐν σοὶ, σκότος ἐστὶ, τὸ σκότος πόσον;

pass_b_english: The eye is the lamp of the body (Matthew 6:22). So if your eye is sound, your whole body will be full of light; but if your eye is evil, your whole body will be dark. And if the light in you is darkness, how great is that darkness (Matthew 6:23)? The sound eye is sincere love, through which, when the whole body is enlightened, love brings forth through the outward parts the same things as the things thought within. The evil eye, on the other hand, is pretended love, which is also called hypocrisy, and through it the whole body of a person is darkened.

problems.quote: when it brings forth through its outward parts the same things as the things thought within
problems.source_quote: δι' ἧς ὅταν τὸ σῶμα φωτίζηται, τὰ αὐτὰ τοῖς ἔσωθεν νοουμένοις, καὶ διὰ τῶν ἔξωθεν μερῶν προφέρουσα
problems.why: Misconstrued syntax: 'προφέρουσα' is feminine singular, agreeing with 'ἀγάπη' (love brings forth), not 'σῶμα' (body). English makes 'body' the subject.
problems.fix: through which, when the body is enlightened, love brings forth through outward parts the same things as thought within
problems.ruling: προφέρουσα is fem. sg. agreeing with ἀγάπη, not σῶμα (neut.). Love brings forth, not body. English misleads.

edits.old: through which the body is enlightened when it brings forth through its outward parts the same things as the things thought within
edits.new: through which, when the body is enlightened, love brings forth through the outward parts the same things as the things thought within

problems.quote: The sound eye is sincere love, through which, when the body is enlightened
problems.source_quote: δι' ἧς ὅταν τὸ σῶμα φωτίζηται
problems.why: Missing 'the whole body' (ὅλον τὸ σῶμα implied from prior); more critically, the Greek asks a question with προφέρουσα; (a question mark in source), but English makes it a statement.
problems.fix: The sound eye is unhypocritical love, through which, when the whole body is enlightened, does it not bring forth through the outward parts the same things as are thought within?
problems.ruling: Source προφέρουσα; has question mark; English makes it a statement, changing meaning and misleading reader.

edits.old: The sound eye is sincere love, through which, when the body is enlightened, love brings forth through the outward parts the same things as the things thought within.
edits.new: The sound eye is sincere love, through which, when the whole body is enlightened, does it not bring forth through the outward parts the same things as the things thought within?

fixed: Changed the statement to a question and added 'whole' to match the source's question mark and implied 'whole body'.

problems.quote: does it not bring forth through the outward parts the same things as the things thought within
problems.source_quote: τὰ αὐτὰ τοῖς ἔσωθεν νοούμενοις, καὶ διὰ τῶν ἔξωθεν μερῶν προφέρουσα
problems.why: Greek has participles agreeing with ἀγάπη (love brings forth), not a question expecting 'yes'; the rhetorical question changes grammar and sense.
problems.fix: love brings forth through the outward parts the same things as are thought within.
problems.ruling: προφέρουσα is a participle modifying ἀγάπη, not an interrogative. Rendering as a question misrepresents the grammar.

problems.quote: when the whole body is enlightened
problems.source_quote: δι' ἧς ὅταν τὸ σῶμα φωτίζηται
problems.why: Missing 'ὅλον' (whole): 'the whole body' not 'the body', changing the scope of enlightenment.
problems.fix: when the whole body is enlightened
problems.ruling: Source says ὅλον τὸ σῶμα (the whole body); English omits ὅλον, narrowing the scope.

edits.old: through which, when the whole body is enlightened, does it not bring forth through the outward parts the same things as the things thought within?
edits.new: through which, when the whole body is enlightened, love brings forth through the outward parts the same things as the things thought within.

fixed: Changed the rhetorical question to a statement with 'love' as the subject, matching the Greek participle agreeing with ἀγάπη.
The omission of 'whole' was already corrected in the current English text; no further change needed.

problems.quote: the light in you is darkness
problems.why: Same verse quoted with different wording; reader may think different verses.

problems.why: Final phrase shifts from 'darkness' to 'transgressions' without marking Gregory's interpretive move.
problems.fix: Clarify that 'how much worse' explains 'how great is the darkness'.

problems.quote: love brings forth through the outward parts the same things as the things thought within
problems.why: 'outward parts' is awkward; likely means 'speech/actions' as opposed to 'parts'.
